novelty.reasoning: Core claims: (1) reasoning length for the current problem is causally shifted by the immediately preceding problem's difficulty/length; (2) this is a cross-problem contamination effect distinct from single-problem length planning; (3) a persistent boundary state/budget vector carries the effect and can be probed/steered; (4) the effect is separable from generic context length/priming. Compared with prior work on single-problem length planning/steering, the cross-problem anchoring setting is a genuine delta and non-trivial, not just an obvious next step. Main novelty risk is that the effect may collapse into generic order/priming or context-length artifacts rather than a distinct length-budget representation.
revision_notes: Explicitly state the minimal novel phenomenon as an order-effect on *reasoning length* holding target problem content fixed, and separate it from accuracy/order effects.
Add one sentence in Related Work contrasting against generic priming, position effects, and context-length fatigue literature, not just length-steering papers.
Tighten the causal claim wording: replace 'carried by a persistent length-budget representation' with 'we test whether a boundary state encodes the carryover'.

impact.reasoning: Behavior/problem: per-item reasoning compute is miscalibrated by neighboring problems in sequence. Who cares: batched evaluation, multi-turn assistants, agent loops, and benchmark designers. If true, downstream changes are real: order-dependent scores, wasted tokens on easy-after-hard cases, under-computation on hard-after-easy cases, and a training-free mitigation path. Strongest one-line case: model compute allocation is path-dependent, so performance and efficiency are artifacts of item order, not just item difficulty.
revision_notes: Add a brief 'Why this matters' paragraph in the abstract emphasizing order-dependent benchmark contamination and deployment cost, not the steering method.
Name the downstream settings explicitly in the title/intro: batched eval, multi-turn chat, agentic loops.
Quantify one concrete consequence in the abstract (e.g., score swing or token waste) to sharpen the so-what test.

review.reasoning: The proposal is testable and structured, but some claims are stronger than the current experimental design can cleanly identify. Biggest gap: dissociating true carryover of a length-budget representation from generic priming, content spillover, and position/context-length effects. The mixed-effects/probing/patching plan is plausible, but the proposal needs sharper falsifiable definitions, more explicit controls, and a clearer prior-work boundary. Venue-readiness is moderate: experiments are feasible, yet acceptance-quality evidence will require careful ablations and stronger negative controls.
revision_notes: Add an exact operational definition of 'length contagion' and primary endpoint(s): e.g., token-count shift on identical target problems across predecessor conditions.
Include stronger controls: matched-content but different-length predecessors, same-length different-difficulty predecessors, shuffled-order baseline, and a no-predecessor separator baseline.
Specify the statistical model in one line (fixed/random effects, primary covariates, correction for model family/task) and pre-register the decisive test for H1.
Add ablations for generic context effects: predecessor answer length vs reasoning length, predecessor correctness vs length, and intervening filler distance.
State how reasoning length is measured across models with different delimiter conventions; include a fallback if think/answer boundaries are ambiguous.
Soften or qualify the mechanistic claim from 'the cause' to 'a candidate causal locus' unless patching plus controls are decisive.
